title: Loft Dynamics and Pathfinder Aviation make H125 VR simulator training available in Alaska
summary: Pathfinder will install Alaska’s first Airbus H125 VR simulator at its main base in Anchorage, Loft Dynamics said.
body_markdown:
[Loft Dynamics](https://www.loftdynamics.com/) announced that[Pathfinder Aviation](https://www.pathfinderaviation.com/) will install Alaska’s first Airbus[H125](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/h125) VR simulator at its main base in Anchorage, giving its pilots year-round access to aircraft-specific training in Alaska.


Pathfinder operates a fleet of 22 helicopters and averages roughly 8,000 flight hours annually, supporting remote operations and precision external-load work across Alaska and the continental United States.


For helicopter operators in Alaska, training often competes with the realities of the job: weather can limit flyable days, winter brings limited daylight, and peak operating periods are also when helicopters are needed most for customer missions.


Most of Pathfinder’s pilots live outside Alaska and travel in for training events, making weather-driven delays even more disruptive.


The simulator is expected to arrive in Anchorage by end of 2026, and Pathfinder plans to begin using it immediately for proficiency and mission training.


“Helicopter pilots often do their most demanding work in places where consistent simulator access is hardest to come by,” said Sebastien Borel, CEO of Loft Dynamics.


Loft Dynamics Photo


“Alaska exposes the limits of a training model that depends on good weather, spare aircraft and long-distance travel. Pathfinder is changing the equation by putting[H125](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/h125) training at its base in Anchorage, where pilots can train more often, safely and on their own schedule. The old model asks pilots to go to the simulator. We’re building a future where the simulator comes to the pilots.”


“In Alaska, we don’t get to choose when conditions become difficult, so our pilots need to be ready before they do,” said Rogan Parker, CEO of Pathfinder Aviation.


“The value of having this simulator in Anchorage is repetition. We can put pilots through a whiteout, IIMC event or emergency, work through decision making, then run the scenario again. That kind of repetition is hard to achieve consistently in the aircraft, and it gives pilots the chance to build judgment before the stakes are real.”


Pathfinder plans to use the simulator for inadvertent IMC (IIMC) avoidance, including repeated practice responding to a loss of visual reference and transitioning to instruments; Part 135 emergency procedures; Part 133 external-load operations; normal and abnormal procedures; whiteout conditions; mountain, pinnacle, slope and confined-site operations; and local site and terrain familiarization.


Loft Dynamics Photo


Heli-skiing will be an early focus. Pathfinder’s[H125](https://helitrader.com/for-sale/helicopters/airbus/h125) pilots operate in mountainous, snow-covered terrain where flat light, blowing snow and rapidly changing visibility can complicate landing-zone decisions.


Loft Dynamics is developing scenery based on Pathfinder’s real-world heli-ski operating areas in the Chugach Mountains, including the Valdez/Thompson Pass region and north Cordova, allowing pilots to familiarize themselves with local terrain and landing sites before flying those missions.


The simulator will initially support Pathfinder’s internal pilot group. Pathfinder plans to integrate it into recurrent and seasonal training and, as local demand develops, make it available to other helicopter operators and pilots in the region.


The Anchorage installation builds on Loft Dynamics’ work with operators including[Air Greenland](https://www.loftdynamics.com/air-greenland-why-vr-flight-training-is-critical-even-at-the-top-of-the-world/) and[Helitrans Norge](https://www.loftdynamics.com/norways-largest-domestic-helicopter-operator-helitrans-uses-the-worlds-first-of-its-kind-airbus-h125-vr-simulator-for-helicopter-training/) , bringing aircraft-specific training closer to pilots in places where distance, weather and geography can make frequent training harder to access.


Pathfinder plans to pursue FAA Level 7 flight training device qualification for the simulator. It will use the device for proficiency and mission training before qualification. Once qualified, Pathfinder would plan to incorporate available FAA training credits into its formal training programs.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by Loft Dynamics.*
